commits.edited_message:
Fix stale XMT OD link on SFNode replacement

A node replaced in an SFNode field kept its OD link, which was then
dereferenced at end of parse.

While at it, stop discarding OD links whose descriptor is already
assigned when a scene replace unwinds a PROTO declaration: such a link
may also carry URLs of the outer scene, which are still resolved at end
of parse. Links waiting for their descriptor are dropped as before.

Scope XMT peeked nodes to their scene graph

A USE could bind to a DEF of another scene graph. Also restrict the
recursive OD-link sweep over deferred DEF nodes to sub-graphs owned by
a proto instance: a DEF node of the main graph drops its OD links when
detached from the tree, so the sweep cannot find anything there.

coupling:
The defect lives in the XMT-A OD-link lifetime machinery of src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c and is split across two edited commits; neither edit produces a reachable memory error on its own.

Background: xmt_parse_url() records a raw MFURL* (field storage inside a live node) on parser->od_links for every url="od:N". When a scene replace is parsed while a PROTO declaration is open (parser->parsing_proto), xmt_parse_command() first drops the pending od_links, then unwinds the proto, then sweeps parser->def_nodes: each DEF node with num_instances==1 gets xmt_remove_od_links_recursive() and is afterwards released with gf_node_unregister() (freeing the node and its subtree, including any node that owns a linked MFURL). At end of parse xmt_resolve_od_links() dereferences every surviving MFURL* whose link has an assigned descriptor.

Edit 1 (d2c67f1, 'Fix stale XMT OD link on SFNode replacement') relaxes the od_links flush that accompanies the PROTO unwind: links whose descriptor is already assigned are now kept (only unassigned links are dropped), on the rationale that an assigned link may also carry URLs of nodes of the outer scene which are still resolved at end of parse. On its own this is safe: the def_nodes sweep that runs a few lines later still strips the links recursively before the deferred DEF nodes are freed.

Edit 2 (0e0a556, 'Scope XMT peeked nodes to their scene graph') narrows that def_nodes sweep: the recursive OD-link removal is skipped for DEF nodes whose scene graph is not owned by a proto instance (pOwningProto unset), on the rationale that a main-graph DEF node already drops its OD links when it is detached from the tree. That claim is only true because of the SFNode-replacement cleanup d2c67f1 added - and only when the node's num_instances is 1 at detach time. On its own this edit is also safe: the flush from edit 1's site (still the original unconditional drop in the tree without edit 1) has already removed every od_link, so the skipped sweep has nothing left to miss.

Composition: a MovieTexture with url="od:5" (OD 5 declared earlier, so the link is assigned) sits inside an Appearance carrying DEF="D". A second <appearance> element replaces D in the Shape's SFNode field; D survives the replacement (num_instances 2: parent + def_nodes, so d2c67f1's own cleanup guard skips it) and is left referenced only by parser->def_nodes. A later scene replace parsed while a ProtoDeclare is open then hits the relaxed flush (edit 1 keeps the assigned link alive) followed by the scoped sweep (edit 2 skips D because D belongs to the main graph) and the deferred DEF release, which frees D and with it the MovieTexture holding the linked MFURL. xmt_resolve_od_links() then reads the_url->count and rewrites url->url/OD_ID through the dangling MFURL* - a heap-use-after-free (ASan aborts in xmt_resolve_od_links, free traced to the def_nodes release in xmt_parse_command).

Why the fix is non-local: reverting edit 1 alone restores the unconditional flush, so no od_link survives the PROTO unwind and the scoped sweep of edit 2 has nothing to miss; reverting edit 2 alone restores the unconditional recursive sweep, which strips the surviving link of edit 1 before the deferred DEF node is freed. A correct fix must reason about both commits together (e.g. keep the sweep unconditional, or make the flush drop links that point into deferred DEF nodes) - patching either commit's diff in isolation leaves a memory-safe loader.
